LOPE validates the node: healthcare education capacity is not only online courseware; it includes off-campus lab sites, skills/simulation equipment, mixed reality, prerequisite strategies, class scheduling, and partner-university infrastructure.
CAE is a plausible but diluted simulation-equipment supplier; keep it in the underfollowed lane only if current filings confirm meaningful healthcare simulation exposure.

Many apparent pure-play nursing simulation suppliers such as Laerdal, Gaumard, Anatomage, and BioDigital appear private or not clearly US-listed; public-market exposure may be indirect through platform operators, clinical-placement software, 3D medical-model vendors, or diversified simulation companies.

node: Healthcare education capacity: ABSN, OTA, nursing simulation, VR, lab infrastructure, and clinical-placement enablement
summary: Layer 1B expands the healthcare-education capacity node beyond obvious online-learning and university operators. The strongest directly evidenced public-market exposures are Grand Canyon Education as a healthcare cohort-capacity operator and HealthStream as a clinical-placement/workforce-compliance software vendor. CAE is a plausible equipment/simulation supplier because its public materials describe healthcare simulation markets, but its exposure is diluted by aviation and defense. 3D Systems is a lower-confidence speculative shadow candidate: it has healthcare, surgical-planning, anatomic-model, and medical-education capabilities, but its direct linkage to nursing/allied-health cohort expansion is weaker and requires revenue/customer verification.
